[Development blog](https://bwalletx.com/blog) · 013 · 29 Sep – 5 Oct 2026

# Two sites from one

A download page became bwallet.space, then bwalletx.com became the main site, with the store site generated from it. And this blog.

## From a download page to two sites

The first site, on 29 September, was a download page for the Yours-branded port, with an Android APK and a TestFlight link. On 1 October it became the bWallet site at bwallet.space, with section videos, a beta APK and a waitlist.

On 3 October we forked it to make bwalletx.com. Over the next two days bwalletx.com became the main site, with pages for features, Exchange, Social, Agents, Strategies, CLI, MCP, Android, iPhone, Extension, Developers and PNEEs, each with its own share image.

## Keeping the store site clean

bwallet.space is the site for the store app, and it must not advertise features the store app doesn't have. Since 4 October a script copies the shared assets from bwalletx.com and generates the bwallet.space home page from ours, with trading, token rooms and social sign-in taken out and clear links to bwalletx.com. Pages that exist only on bWalletX redirect there. The script never copies HTML pages, so this blog is not copied to the store site.

## Navigation

The navbar was rewritten by hand on every page until 5 October, when one script, `nav.js`, started rendering it from a single config for both sites. Each section can have its own sub-menu. That is where this blog lives: under Developers.

## Small things that went wrong

- The waitlist form 404'd on bwalletx.com until we proxied it to bwallet.space.

- X kept old share images, so several images have version numbers in their file names to break the cache.

- The big b logo was hidden under the fixed header on sub-pages until we added spacing.

- We dropped a Brave Shields tip from the extension page because we hadn't verified it.

## About this blog

These posts were written from the git history of the wallet, this site, the chat server and the PNEEs prototype. They are as accurate as the commits allow. If something here is wrong, the code is the record, and we will correct the post.

## What's not done

- The two sites still share one API host; bwalletx.com proxies some requests to bwallet.space.
- The APK download folder keeps every version; there is no cleanup yet.

Related: [Home](https://bwalletx.com/) · [Features](https://bwalletx.com/features) · [Developers](https://bwalletx.com/developers)

# Development blog

How bWallet and bWalletX were built, one chapter at a time. Every post is written from the git history of the wallet, this site, the chat server and the PNEEs prototype. It covers what we built, why, what broke, what we reversed and what is still not done.

Newest first. Dates come from commits. bWallet is a fork of [Yours Wallet](https://github.com/yours-org/yours-wallet) (MIT licence).

# Privacy Policy

bWalletX (Beta) · Effective 1 October 2026

bWalletX is published by The Bitcoin Corporation Ltd and is based on the open-source Yours Wallet (MIT licence).
It is not made, reviewed or endorsed by the Yours Wallet authors, and this policy covers only the bWalletX mobile
app.

## Summary

bWalletX is non-custodial. We run no servers for the app and don't operate accounts. We don't collect your name,
email, contacts, location, advertising identifiers, analytics or crash reports. Your private keys and recovery
phrase never leave your device.

## What stays on your device

-
Your private keys and recovery phrase, encrypted with a key derived from your password and stored in the iOS
Keychain (this device only, excluded from iCloud and device backups) or in Android storage encrypted with an
Android Keystore key (excluded from Google backups).

-
If you turn on Face ID, Touch ID or fingerprint unlock, a key to unlock your wallet is sealed behind your
device's biometrics. Your biometric data itself is handled by the operating system and is never available to
the app.

- Settings, recent sites and apps you open, chat history cached for bChat, and local caches.

## What the app sends over the network

To work as a wallet, the app connects to these third-party services, all over HTTPS:

-
Wallet storage: by default, your wallet's transaction records (outputs, transactions and related
metadata, not your private keys) are synced to a remote wallet storage service operated by 1Sat
(`wallet.1sat.app`). You can change the storage provider in Settings → Wallet Backup.

-
Blockchain services: address, balance, transaction and token lookups, and transaction broadcasts, go to
BSV indexing services (1Sat APIs). Transaction links open on WhatsOnChain.

- Wallet messaging: wallet-to-wallet messages use `messagebox.1sat.app`.

-
Market, Media, Apps and Chat: trending tokens, collections, listings and ordinal media are loaded from
1Sat indexing and content services (ORDFS). The Apps tab lists bApps such as bChat, bMovies and bWriter; bChat
and other bApps you open talk to their own services, which receive what you send them.

-
Names and payments to names: when you send to a $handle, paymail or OpNS name, or look up your own
name, the app asks 1Sat indexers (including OpNS), bit-sign and HandCash paymail lookup services to resolve
that name to a payment destination. Those services see the name being looked up.

-
Market and Chat: token and NFT listings, media and token rooms are loaded from 1Sat indexers. The
Market's safety filter runs as part of that loading; if you use Report, the item is hidden on your device and,
where a review service is configured, the item reference is sent to us for review.

-
Websites you open in the in-app browser receive the requests you make and the responses you approve.
They're governed by their own privacy policies.

These services see your IP address and the public blockchain data needed to answer each request. Blockchain
transactions are public by nature.

## Verified identity (KYC certificates)

Identity verification is optional. If you choose to verify, you are sent to bit-sign, which uses Veriff to check
your identity document. bit-sign and Veriff keep the verification record under their own privacy policies.
bit-sign then issues a private certificate that is stored in your wallet on your device. bWalletX does not upload
that certificate anywhere by itself: you choose which details, if any, to reveal to an app or service, and only
when you approve it.

## Notifications

If you allow notifications, the app shows local alerts about incoming transactions. They're generated on your
device; no push notification service is used.

## Testing waitlist (this website)

If you join the testing waitlist on this website, we collect your email address, the phone platform you chose
(iPhone, Android or Either), the time you signed up, and your browser's user-agent string (to help spot abuse).
This is stored by The Bitcoin Corporation Ltd in our own database and is used only to invite you to test bWalletX
and send testing updates. We do not sell it or share it for marketing. You can unsubscribe from any email, or
ask us to delete your entry at any time using the contact details below.

## Your choices

- You can delete all app data by signing out in Settings, or by uninstalling the app.

- You can turn biometric unlock off from the lock screen at any time.

- You can change the remote wallet storage provider in Settings → Wallet Backup.

## Children

The app is not directed at children under 13.

## Changes

We'll post changes to this policy on this page, and in the source repository at
[github.com/b0ase/yours-mobile](https://github.com/b0ase/yours-mobile).

## Contact

Questions about this mobile app: open an issue at
[github.com/b0ase/yours-mobile/issues](https://github.com/b0ase/yours-mobile/issues).
